content.intro: This lesson covers Synchronous and Asynchronous Execution. It sits in Module 17, Asynchronous Rust, and builds toward a practical Rust mental model rather than memorizing a term in isolation.
content.why_it_matters: Synchronous and Asynchronous Execution matters when you work with future execution and runtime boundaries. Understanding the rule helps you predict compiler or runtime behavior, document assumptions, and choose a safer implementation when inputs or system conditions change.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: An async function creates a Future. The future makes progress only when polled by an executor; the async syntax itself does not choose a runtime or guarantee parallel execution.

content_blocks.title: A reliable way to reason about it
content_blocks.text: For Synchronous and Asynchronous Execution, write down the inputs, the guarantee you expect, and the boundary where that guarantee stops. Work through a minimal example first; then deliberately test one edge case. Async Rust is a language model built around Future; a runtime provides execution, timers, networking, and scheduling services as needed.
